intended_object: The Fischer (Bombieri-type) inner product ⟨p,q⟩ = Σ_α α! p_α q_α on the space of real polynomials in (r+1)·n variables that are multihomogeneous of row degrees λ, packaged as an `InnerProductSpace.Core`. Inferred from the name, the docstring and the definition of `coefficientEmbedding`.
explanation:
The definition pulls back the Euclidean inner product along an injective linear map. That map is `youngMultihomogeneousCoefficientEmbedding`: it includes the multihomogeneous subspace into the homogeneous polynomials of total degree Σλ_i, then sends p to the vector (√(α!)·coeff_α p)_α in `EuclideanSpace ℝ (DegreeIndex …)`. The resulting inner product is ⟨p,q⟩ = Σ_α α!·p_α·q_α, which is the standard Fischer inner product restricted to this subspace. Because the map is injective, the form is positive definite, as `InnerProductSpace.Core` requires.

The setting (real coefficients, the specific multihomogeneous subspace) is the one the library's argument about spherical codes needs. Over ℝ, the Fischer form is the standard one, and restricting it to this subspace is the point of the definition, so it is not too narrow.

Mathlib has no Fischer inner product on polynomials, so there is no counterpart. The definition is partly a device for building an instance, but it does define a recognisable mathematical inner product, and it does so correctly.
